newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rolls-Rolls sees Asia revenues rising - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Rolls-Rolls sees Asia revenues rising - CEO.

text.p: Aero-engine maker Rolls-Royce Plc expects Asia's contribution to overall revenues to rise to 30 percent over the next five years from 20 percen now, chief executive John Rose said on Wednesday.
Rose, who flew into Singapore for the delivery of the first Rolls-Royce Trent-powered Boeing 777 to Singapore Airlines Ltd, said Asia currently accounts for "30 percent of the group's order book".
He told a news conference the Rolls-Royce order book currently stood at US$11.2 billion with another $1 billion which has been announced but has not yet contracted.
Rose also said the company was in talks with SIA and others in region for various business opportunities, but he declined to give details.
Earlier in the year, Rolls-Royce and SIA set up a joint venture for a component repair and overhaul centre in Singapore.
